plain_text:
"Gemini gave you the feeling that they could do
anything you wanted," Oldenburg said in Artists at
Gemini G.E.L.: Celebrating the 25th Year. In 1968 he
had asked if Gemini would be interested in producing
a print with a sculptural component. "It was almost
like the way we started Gemini," Felsen told the
Smithsonian. "We had no idea what we were doing,
but we said, 'Sure'." It certainly helped that LA had
dozens of prototype shops for the movie and aero-
space industries. The edition, Profile Airflow, was
a lithograph depicting the outline of a 1936 Chrys-
ler Airflow overlaid with a soft, translucent rubbery
relief of the car, fabricated with help from a Disney
mold maker, in swimming pool teal.

plain_text:
In his photographs, Felsen records the energy
and dedication of the artists and the power of their
collaborations with master printers and fabrica-
tors. The work of creating a print is a "give-and-take,
experimental, passionate, exhausting time," he said.
"I really saw...the spirit of what it is to be creative and
how demanding it is and how much effort has to go
into it." He captures the hard work, both the labor
and joy, of creating the new. "What's unique about
Gemini—the doors are completely open for the artist
to do whatever they want," says master printer, Jill
Lerner. "It's a place where creativity runs free."
